facts.text: Kindersley was incorporated in 1910 and named after Sir Robert Kindersley, a major shareholder in the Canadian Northern Railway.
The town sits beside Motherwell Reservoir, where Kindersley Regional Park was founded in 1968 and offers a 9‑hole grass‑greens golf course.
In 2004, Kindersley was chosen as the launch site for the da Vinci Project, Canada's entry for the Ansari X Prize, though the flight never took place.
The town’s climate is semi‑arid, with winters that are long, cold and dry, while summers are short and warm, and precipitation averages only 325 mm annually.
Kindersley sells its treated municipal wastewater to a local oilfield service company for use in hydraulic fracturing, linking the town to the Bakken shale oil and gas play.
